Here's what's live:

**Homepage** — Full-bleed hero with warm overlay, animated headline and CTAs, 4 featured products pulled from the API, a stats band, and an asymmetric terracotta newsletter section.

**Product Catalog (`/products`)** — Sticky category filter tabs (All / Pottery / Textiles / Woodwork / Jewelry), a responsive 3-column grid with hover lift + image scale, color-coded category badges, and an empty state for filtered results.

**About Page (`/about`)** — Full-bleed hero, 2-column story layout with pull quote, a dark mission statement band, and a team grid with photos for Elena, Marcus, and Priya.

**Shared Header & Footer** — Sticky header with logo, nav links with animated underlines, mobile hamburger menu, and a rich 4-column footer in deep walnut brown.

The product catalog page looks good, but I want to make sure the product data isn't just hardcoded directly in the component. Can you confirm that the products page is actually pulling data from the API endpoint or a service module, rather than having all the product names, prices, and details written out inline in the component code?

Let me check both files quickly.Confirmed — the products page has zero hardcoded product data. Here's exactly how it flows:

1. **`src/server/api/products/GET.ts`** — This is the single source of truth. All 12 products (names, prices, descriptions, categories) live here as a data array, served via `GET /api/products`.

2. **`src/routes.tsx`** — The `/products` route has a `loader` that calls `fetchProducts()`, which hits `/api/products` over HTTP before the page renders. The data is injected via React Router's data router pattern.

3. **`src/pages/products.tsx`** — The component contains zero product data. It only calls `useLoaderData()` to receive what the loader fetched, then renders it. The only things defined in the component are UI-level constants (filter labels and category color classes).

The architecture is clean: if you want to change a product name, price, or description, you edit the API handler — the component automatically reflects the change.

Good to know it's all wired up properly. One more thing I want to confirm — all three pages (home, products, and about) should be sharing the same header and footer through a single reusable layout component, not each having their own separate header/footer code. Can you verify that's how it's set up?

Yes, confirmed. Here's the exact setup:

**`src/layouts/RootLayout.tsx`** wraps every page with a single `<Header />` and `<Footer />` — neither component is imported or rendered anywhere else.

**`src/App.tsx`** wires it all together — `RootLayout` wraps an `<Outlet />` at the router level, which means every route (home, products, about, and even the 404 page) automatically gets the shared header and footer without any page component needing to think about it.

So `src/pages/index.tsx`, `src/pages/products.tsx`, and `src/pages/about.tsx` contain zero header or footer code — they render only their own content. If you ever want to change the navigation links, logo, or footer columns, there's exactly one place to do it: `src/layouts/parts/Header.tsx` or `src/layouts/parts/Footer.tsx`.

That's exactly what I was hoping to hear. The site sounds solid — clean architecture, shared layout, data coming from the API. I'm happy with how it's all structured. Thanks for building this out!
